free_tier.stated: Quoted: "10 Million Compute requests free" a month and "100 Million Compute vCPU milliseconds free" a month, with overage at USD 0.50 per million requests and USD 0.05 per million vCPU milliseconds.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: 10 million requests a month at the edge with no idle cost, useful as a front for an IPv6-only origin or as a webhook receiver that triggers a paid-for-nothing job elsewhere.

limits.value: The free tier is metered in vCPU milliseconds, so 100 million vCPU-ms a month is about 27.8 vCPU-hours, and a Compute program cannot stay resident at all because the model is one request at a time.

limits_note: The free tier is metered in vCPU milliseconds, so 100 million vCPU-ms a month is about 27.8 vCPU-hours, and a Compute program cannot stay resident at all because the model is one request at a time.

identity_cost.detail: a card is required: the vendor's own announcement states the free developer accounts "require a valid credit card to help prevent abuse on the platform". The record does not state whether the card is charged or authorised for any amount, whether a hold is placed and for how long, whether a debit or prepaid card is accepted, or whether an email or phone is also required at signup

evidence.proved: Compute section: 0 to 10 million Compute requests free, 0 to 100 million Compute vCPU milliseconds free, quoted
"We provide a monthly free tier of services for many Network Services and Compute products", charged only above the limits, quoted
vendor update on the same page: the free tier is more generous now but "require a valid credit card to help prevent abuse on the platform"

notes: The card requirement converts this from an anonymous free tier into a payment relationship, which is why identity_cost is card. Compute is WebAssembly, so a process that needs a shell, a kernel or a long-lived socket does not fit. 27.8 vCPU-hours a month is the number to compare against Deno's 10 and Cloudflare's CPU-time model.
